html:
In the early 1930s Australian gold prospectors led by Michael Leahy walked into the New Guinea Highlands and found densely farmed valleys home to about a million people unknown to the outside world.

Outsiders had thought the mountainous interior was empty. Highlanders, who had never seen white people, thought the newcomers might be spirits of the dead. Leahy filmed and photographed the meetings, which were often tense and sometimes violent.

Patrol posts, missions and airstrips followed, and the Highlands entered the colonial economy, later growing coffee for export. People who had farmed at Kuk for thousands of years were drawn into a state within one lifetime. See also Territory of Papua and Somare.
sum: In the early 1930s Australian gold prospectors led by Michael Leahy walked into the New Guinea Highlands and found densely farmed valleys home to about a million people unknown to the outside world.
